uncited: It differs from its parent [Spread-space MIP chain with luminance weighting](9093-spread-space-mip-chain-with-luminance-weighting.md) by adding a luminance-weighted mask to prevent illumination leaking artifacts that can occur when naively applying this blur to high-contrast scenes.
Initialize base level $k=0$ with input radiance $\mathbb{L}_{\text{sc}}^{[0]}$ and width $\mathbb{W}^{[0]}$.
Controls the distance/width below which pixels are suppressed.
Small positive values create a sharp cutoff; larger values create a softer transition.
- If $\mathbb{W}^{[k-1]}$ is uniformly below $T$, the mask becomes zero, and the MIP level becomes black.
This is intended behavior to prevent leaking.
- Precision issues may arise if $T$ is very small or $\varepsilon$ is extremely small, leading to binary masking rather than smooth weighting.

- The definition of $\mathbb{W}$ (spreading width) must be consistent with the parent method [Spread-space MIP chain with luminance weighting](9093-spread-space-mip-chain-with-luminance-weighting.md).
- **Time Complexity:** Building each MIP level requires one mask computation (pixel-wise smoothstep) and one Gaussian convolution.
The convolution cost depends on kernel size.
Overall, linear in the number of pixels per level.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing an additional mask texture $\mathbb{M}^{[k]}$ at each level, or recomputing it on the fly if memory is constrained.
The choice of $T$ and $\varepsilon$ can affect visual quality and may require tuning.
- **When to use:** When using Gaussian MIP map blurring for real-time light transport or scattering, and illumination leaking artifacts are visible.
- **When not to use:** If the scene has uniform luminance or if the cost of maintaining the mask is prohibitive.
Originated in the context of real-time light transport in analytically integrable participating media.
It addresses the issue of sharp discontinuities and incorrect light leaking seen in naive MIP map filtering approaches.
